To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
peroxisomes contain a nafenopin-coenzyme A (CoA) ligase that is distinct from the peroxisosmal long-chain fatty acid-CoA synthetase.
nafenopion-CoA formation is mediated by an enzyme that differs from the peroxidase long chain fatty acid ligase in relation its xenobiotic inhibitor profile and kinetic charateristics.

nafenopion-CoA formation in peroxisomes is catalysed predominantly by a high affinity, low capacity enzyme, that is inhibited by clofibrate but not by antibodies raised against microsomal palmtioyl-CoA ligase, that is not a member of the microsomal long chain fatty acyl-CoA synthetase family, and that is inhibited by palmitic acid, ibuprofen, ciprofibrate and clofibric aci.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a novel xenobiotic-CoA ligase which is localized within peroxisomes and may be involved in peroxisomal fatty acid beta-oxidation.
the identification and characterisation of a novel xenobiotic metabolising enzyme in peroxisomes.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms by which peroxisomes respond to xenobiotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nafenopin metabolising system in the rat is not identical to the peroxisome proliferator activated receptor alpha (PPAR alpha) system.
the rat liver peroxisosomal nafenopion-CoA ligase is a distinct entity, which may be related to the cytosolic CoA ligases.

the peroxisomes of rat liver catalyse the CoA esterification of nafenopidin and the reaction is catalysed, at least in part, by an apparent high affinity, low capacity, xenobiotic-sensitive peroxisomal isoform which differs from the long chain fatty acid ligase in relation, for example, to its inhibitor and kinetic characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rat hepatic microsomal and peroxisomal xenobiotic-CoA ligase activities are mediated by multiple isozymes.
rat hepatic microsomes catalyse a number of reactions with nafenopin including N-demethylation, N-hydroxylation, N-glucuronidation, N-acyl glucuronidation and N-acyl sulphation.
peroxisomal fatty acid-CoA synthesis in rat liver is catalysed in a manner that is distinct from that of the microsomal enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peroxisome proliferators are a diverse group of compounds with a wide range of effects on the cell.
peroxisomal enzymes are not only involved in the metabolism of fatty acids but also in the metabolism of a number of xenobiotic substrates.
the nafenopin CoA ligase is a unique peroxisomal protein that is different from the microsomal fatty acid CoA ligase.
